title: Regional switchover controller for zero-downtime Hosted API upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Implement a regional switchover controller and upgrade tooling to enable zero-downtime Hosted API upgrades across regions with deterministic traffic attenuation, LTS channel awareness, and automated rollback triggers.

Background: We have frequent incidents where multi-region upgrades expose edge cases in routing, leading to partial outages or elevated error rates in some regions. Current traffic shifting primitives are ad-hoc and tied to individual deploys. We need a centralized controller that understands version semantics (major/minor/patch + LTS flags), cross-region dependency graphs, and rollout gates tied to SLO/health signals.

Scope:
- Controller service that orchestrates coordinated switchover across regions using a sliding-window traffic attenuation algorithm (percent-based schedule with health gates).
- Support for LTS channels: stable, lts, experimental; ability to prefer LTS builds for enterprise tenants and pin versions per-customer during switchover.
- Integration with runtime-1.21 release pipeline and Redwood Console rollout UI (hooks for visualizing state and manual overrides).
- Upgrade CLI (redwoodctl rollout) to create, preview and promote switchover plans.
- Telemetry and SLI mapping for rollout gates: 99th percentile latency, 5xx rate, token-throughput variance, downstream error amplification.
- Automatic rollback policies and a "lifeboat" fallback route that routes traffic to the last-known-good variant in case of severe health degradation.

Non-goals: Full rework of scheduler/k8s autoscaler or replacing existing per-region autoscaling. We won't change model variant packaging or image build pipelines in this ticket.

Design notes:
- Versioning: controller uses semver-like tags and an LTS boolean. Each deployment publishes a manifest with version, variant-id, compatible-kernel-hash, and capacity profile. Controller validates compatibility before scheduling traffic.
- Traffic attenuation: schedule expressed as array of steps (time-window, target-percentage). Controller applies per-gateway roll rates with jitter to avoid synchronized cutovers.
- Health gates: windowed anomaly detector compares current SLI to baseline using a short-term median absolute deviation. If gate fails for >2 consecutive windows, controller pauses and triggers automated mitigation.
- Policy engine: supports global policies (SLO thresholds), tenant exceptions (enterprise LTS pinning), and manual holdpoints with runbook references.

Migration plan: Start with a single non-critical region (eu-west-3) and synthetic load test. Then roll to secondary regions (us-west-2, eu-central-1) with staged ramp. After 2 successful runs, enable for a small percentage of production traffic for Canary customers, then full rollout.

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/designs/regional-switchover-controller (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/9123
- Console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1SwitchoverUI
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller can create and execute a regional switchover plan that moves 100% of traffic from version A to version B with no increase in 99th percentile latency beyond configured SLO for >5 minutes.
2) LTS channel selection works: enterprise tenants with 'lts' flag remain on pinned LTS versions during a default switchover.
3) Automated rollback triggers on: 5xx rate >0.5% absolute increase OR 99p latency regression >30% sustained for 2 windows.
4) redwoodctl rollout preview shows a dry-run with region-by-region timeline and estimated impact.
5) Console displays plan state, per-region health metrics, and provides manual pause/rollback actions.
6) Two successful canary runs in non-prod and one controlled production run with traffic shaping completed without manual intervention.
tasks:
- Build controller API and state machine for plan lifecycle (create/preview/execute/pause/rollback).
- Implement traffic attenuation engine with per-gateway jitter and rate limits.
- Add LTS-aware version resolver and tenant pinning hooks.
- Integrate health signal collectors and gate evaluator.
- Expose CLI commands and Console UI endpoints.
- Add telemetry dashboards and alerting rules for rollout health.
- Write runbooks and automated post-mortem templates.
risks:
- False positives in anomaly detector could unnecessarily rollback a healthy deployment. Mitigation: conservative thresholds initially, manual approval step for high-risk tenants.
- Cross-region dependencies (datastore migrations) may cause latent failures unrelated to serving. Mitigation: dependency discovery step in preview and explicit blocking rules.
- Edge gateways may have different throttling behaviors causing uneven traffic distribution. Mitigation: per-gateway calibration and runtime profiling before production run.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Asha Patel: Initial spec posted to Confluence. Prototype controller skeleton in the infra repo. Asked SRE to validate telemetry readiness.
2026-02-28 - Jordan Kim: Confirmed the EU gateways support per-route gradual weights. Requested adding 99p tokenization latency as a signal.
2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented the plan state machine and CLI preview. Pushed draft PR (linked). Marking for early test in eu-west-3.
2026-03-09 - Priya Verma: Console team built mock for manual override buttons; need API contract for pause/force-rollback endpoints.
2026-03-10 - Mina Lopez: Suggested adding a 'maintenance-window' flag to prevent rollouts during scheduled infra work. Added to tasks.
notes: Implementation should prioritize observability and safety over rollout speed. Begin with a tolerant default policy and make policies stricter as we gain confidence. Document default thresholds and provide easy knobs for product and SRE to tune per-release.
follow_up: 1) Post-release: collect a runbook-driven postmortem template for any non-zero deviation from expected SLOs. 2) Future work: integrate model-variant compatibility checks with kernel-selection hints to avoid silent performance regressions.
